name: clock_nanosleep
synopsis: int clock_nanosleep(clockid_t clockid, int flags, const struct timespec *t, struct timespec *_Nullable remain);
description: clock_nanosleep() allows a thread to sleep for a specified interval with nanosecond precision, using a chosen clock. It supports both relative and absolute time specifications, and can return the remaining time if interrupted.

parameters.name: clockid
parameters.description: Specifies the clock to use for measuring the sleep interval, such as CLOCK_REALTIME or CLOCK_MONOTONIC.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to indicate if the time is relative (0) or absolute (TIMER_ABSTIME).

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: Pointer to a timespec structure specifying the sleep interval or absolute time.

parameters.name: remain
parameters.description: If not NULL and flags is not TIMER_ABSTIME, stores the remaining unslept time if the call is interrupted.

return_value.failure: Returns a positive error number on failure

errors.description: t or remain specified an invalid address.
The sleep was interrupted by a signal handler.
The value in the tv_nsec field was not in the range [0, 999999999], tv_sec was negative, or clockid was invalid.
The kernel does not support sleeping against this clockid.
